{"sample_id": "blind-ca5d00d65d7a45028231e1f9fad5137b", "theorem": "Let \( N \) be a positive integer. Two persons play the following game. The first player writes a list of positive integers not greater than \( 25 \), not necessarily different, such that their sum is at least \( 200 \). The second player wins if he can select some of these numbers so that their sum \( S \) satisfies the condition \( 200-N \leq S \leq 200+N \). What is the smallest value of \( N \) for which the second player has a winning strategy?", "assumptions": [], "domain": "baltic_mo", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

To show that \(N=10\) is insufficient, let the first player write four \(25\)'s, four \(22\)'s, and one \(23\). Their total is
\[
4\cdot25+4\cdot22+23=211.
\]
Every proper subset omits at least one number, all of which are at least \(22\), so its sum is at most \(211-22=189\). The full list has sum \(211\). Hence no subset sum belongs to \([190,210]\), proving that \(N\ge 11\).

Now consider any permitted list with total at least \(200\). Among all subsets whose sums are at least \(189\), choose one with minimum sum \(s\). Such a subset exists because the whole list has sum at least \(200\).

For every selected number \(a\), minimality implies
\[
s-a<189.
\]
Since \(a\le 25\),
\[
s<189+a\le214.
\]
As \(s\) is an integer, \(189\le s\le213\).

If \(s=212\), then \(212-a<189\), so every selected number satisfies \(a>23\), hence is \(24\) or \(25\). At most eight such numbers have sum at most \(200\), while at least nine have sum at least \(216\), so their sum cannot be \(212\).

If \(s=213\), then \(213-a<189\), so every selected number satisfies \(a>24\), hence equals \(25\). Their sum is therefore divisible by \(25\), and cannot equal \(213\).

Thus \(189\le s\le211\), equivalently
\[
200-11\le s\le200+11.
\]
Therefore \(N=11\) is sufficient, while the construction above shows that no smaller value works. Hence the required smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\)."}
